articles.author: Murabyte
articles.description:
Disclosure: I make ZebraSheet at Murabyte, which is mentioned below.
If you print Zebra labels from a spreadsheet, you know the pain. The free tool from Zebra does not read Excel files. Full label software like BarTender can cost hundreds of dollars. Here are the practical options.
Word mail merge works for sheet labels, but not for thermal printers that expect ZPL. It is fine for office printers, not for a Zebra roll.
You can build ZPL strings in Excel with formulas, then send them to the printer as raw text. It is free and exact, but you must learn ZPL and test every layout by trial and error.
Tools like BarTender give a visual designer, database connections and many printer drivers. They are powerful. They are also priced for companies, and often more than a small shop needs.
ZebraSheet is a Windows desktop app I built for this one job: open an Excel or CSV file, design the label, add barcode or QR fields, and print one label per row. It works offline and produces ZPL output matching the on-screen preview. It costs $49 one-time, and there is a free trial with a limited number of labels so you can test with your own data first.
Product page: https://murabyte.gumroad.com/l/zebrasheet
https://murabyte.gumroad.com/l/zebrasheet-trial
A few labels, once: mail merge or a free tool.
You know ZPL and want full control: Excel formulas.
Hundreds of rows from a spreadsheet, regularly: a purpose-built tool or full label software.
Whatever you use, print a test label on your own printer and roll before running a big batch.
articles.title: How to print Zebra labels from Excel without expensive software

articles.description:
For signed customer-support documents, start with server-mediated uploads. The backend can enforce identity, allocate a unique object key, record an explicit deletion deadline, and keep browser CORS out of the trust boundary. Move to presigned browser uploads only after verifying the exact bucket and provider configuration in every region you will use.
Short answer: presigned uploads are the better data path for large files, but they are not automatically the safer setup. Retention is a database and lifecycle problem; deletion is a job that needs evidence. For this workload, an upload is not complete until the object key and deleteAfter timestamp are committed together.
The tempting design is React to object storage, followed by a small callback to Node.js. It removes a hop. It also makes …
articles.title: Browser Uploads for User Documents — Direct or Server-Mediated Object Storage

articles.author: Ziwei (Ekko) Yu
articles.description:
Island Evolution is a small order puzzle: you place 8 items on an empty island, and after each placement everything already on the island grows one level. The order you pick decides how far each thing gets. It's built in Godot 4 and runs in the browser.
Eight items means 8! = 40,320 possible orders. That sounds like a lot until you notice a computer can play all of them in a moment. So I did, and the result changed how I balanced the game.
The first decision was to keep the rules out of the code. Every item, level and condition lives in a JSON file. A tree, for example, goes sprout → sapling when water is at least 1 → big tree at water 2 → forest at water 3.
The engine just reads that file and runs a lookup-driven state machine. Nothing about the 8 specific items is compiled into the logic…
articles.title: I brute-forced all 40,320 orders of my puzzle game, and the table became the design doc

In a workshop in Switzerland, more than two hundred and fifty years ago, three men built a boy who could write. He is small — about as tall as a child sitting down would be, in a red coat, at a little mahogany desk — and he is made of roughly six thousand parts, every one of them brass and steel and patience. articles.description:
When someone finishes drafting a first-floor layout and wants to add a second story or a basement foundation, two naive approaches both break down immediately:
Duplicate the whole plan: the user inherits every kitchen island, coat closet, and bathroom partition from the ground floor and has to delete 40 items before drawing bedroom walls.
Start a blank canvas: the exterior foundation outline and stairwell opening almost never align cleanly with the floor below.
In PlanCaliber, we solved this in a single 200-line module (src/lib/cad/levels.ts) that derives a matched 2nd Story Shell or Basement Shell directly from the planar graph of the main floor in one click. Here are the five geometric invariants that make it work reliably on messy real-world user drawings.

articles.author: Apoorv Darshan
articles.description:
Teddy orders two eggs and a latte. Brulee logs breakfast. Then Teddy asks the question that made this worth showing on screen: “How much protein did I get?”
  
  


Brulee and Teddy are two of the eight Live Voice mascots in Fud AI. For this short, I wanted the mascots to introduce the feature without asking viewers to take a cartoon’s word for what the app did.
A spoken “logged” is easy to miss. In the iPhone recording you can see which foods landed in the diary, then read the same protein total Brulee gives Teddy: 20 grams for this sample breakfast. That gives the follow-up question a purpose: it connects the conversation to something you can inspect.
The café exchange is scripted and voiced with ElevenLabs. The screen recording uses sample data, and the dialogue is captioned so the demo still makes sense on mute. If you’re making a demo of a voice interface, try watching yours with the sound off: can you still tell what changed?
Fud AI source on GitHub

articles.description:
A microVM that can push unlimited bytes through its network interface or its disk can make every other VM on the host slow. Firecracker's answer is a rate limiter on each emulated device, built from token buckets. The configuration is a handful of integers, and it is easy to set them to something that does not mean what you think. This post works through what each field does, using Firecracker's design document, its API specification and the network interface update guide, as of November 2026.
This is about Firecracker. It does not describe how any specific platform, Sandscale included, sets its limits.
Firecracker's VMM thread emulates the VirtIO network and block devices. When the guest sends a packet, the Firecracker I/O thread copies it from the emulated interface to the host TAP devic…
articles.title: Firecracker rate limiters: token buckets for network, disk and entropy, worked through

articles.author: EZENWA CHRISTIAN CHIMEREMEZE
articles.description:
Most apps don't do everything inside a single request. Sending an email, processing an upload, generating a report, syncing with another service, crunching a big dataset — all of that takes time. If you try to do it all inside an HTTP request, responses get slow, servers get overloaded, and things start breaking.
That's why we move slow work into the background.
But here's the catch: moving work to the background doesn't automatically make it reliable. Workers crash. Networks time out. External services go down. And sometimes a task runs twice.
So if you're building background jobs in Python, you have to plan for failure from the start.
In this article, I'll walk through how to design background jobs that actually hold up — how to retry sensibly, how to stop duplicate work with idempotency…
articles.title: Designing Reliable Background Jobs in Python: Retries, Idempotency, and Failure Recovery
